title: Inspector AI Improve writes without preview; route it through the diff modal

sections.what: InspectorHelpers.improveWithAI (static/js/inspector/helpers.ts) sends the LLM result straight to api.updateNode with no preview. The moment the model answers, description, actions, tags, uses, weight, current_state, action_costs and skill_check have already changed in the world. The same codebase already owns a preview widget - shared/diff-modal.ts - and the item library-refresh path uses it (InspectorItemView._refreshFromLibrary in static/js/inspector/item-view.ts, which calls DiffModal.show(...) then api.refreshFromLibrary). Improve is the one AI write path that skips it.
sections.why: An LLM change to authored data is the case that most needs a before/after review: it can silently replace tags, flip actions, or rewrite a value the user believed was protected, and the user never sees it. docs/design/full-entity-editors.md states the rule that the inspector is a projection of the authoritative world model and every edit flows through one validated path; an unseen AI write is the exception that rule exists to prevent. The field-lock UI currently implies protected values while nothing shows what the model actually proposed, so the lock and the write disagree.
sections.how: Route improveWithAI through DiffModal.show(current, incoming, sections, {direction: 'to-world'}) - the same call _refreshFromLibrary already makes. Build current from the node's live properties and incoming from the parsed LLM result through the existing apply() builder; reuse the item section list in item-view.ts and the way/area equivalents. Apply only the sections the user keeps, in a single api.updateNode call so the whole-world undo stack reverts it in one step (routes/saveload.py pushes one snapshot per graph update; undo is whole-world, not diff-based). Keep the existing locked_fields gate in buildPrompt/apply so locked fields never reach the proposal. Do not add a second validator: the accepted update still goes through the same endpoint and engine/trigger_validator.py path.

acceptance.text: Improve never writes to the world before the user approves a diff.
The proposal renders before/after per field through shared/diff-modal.ts; no second modal is added.
Locked fields stay out of the proposal and unchanged on apply.
One accepted apply is one api.updateNode call, so one Undo reverts it.
Item, way, and area Improve all use the shared flow.

custom.browser_ui:
Intended UI home: Select an item, way, or area → inspector → its “Improve with AI” action → shared before/after Diff modal. The world must remain unchanged until the author accepts selected sections.

Current availability: The card records that `improveWithAI` currently calls `updateNode` immediately and plans to reuse `DiffModal.show`; the preview-first flow is not claimed as implemented.

Live steps when available:
1. With an LLM configured, open an item with a description and click “Improve with AI”.
   - expected: the shared diff modal shows proposed fields before and after; cancel closes it with no change to `/api/state`.
2. Reopen the proposal, keep only the description section, drop the other sections, and click Update.
   - expected: only the description changes; dropped sections remain byte-for-byte at their prior values.
3. Lock the item's tags, run Improve again, and inspect the proposal.
   - expected: tags are absent from the diff and unchanged after applying other sections.
4. Apply one accepted section and use toolbar Undo once.
   - expected: the whole accepted apply is one `updateNode` write and one undo restores all pre-apply values.
5. Repeat with one way and one area.
   - expected: all three inspector types use the same Diff modal and preserve each type's locked-field rules.

This section defines intended access and live acceptance. It is not a claim that planned UI exists or works today. Current availability says what is implemented and verified now; the numbered steps say how to reach and test the intended surface once it is available.
